blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Annacis Island

items.t: Annacis Island is an island in the Fraser River in the City of Delta, in the Highway 91 / Alex Fraser Bridge corridor; street access is by Derwent Way, Cliveden Avenue, Eaton Way and Audley Boulevard.

The island is bounded by the Fraser River channels around it (the surrounding channels are called Annacis Channel and Annieville Channel); nearby areas are Nordel and the rest of North Delta to the south across the Alex Fraser Bridge, New Westminster to the north, Richmond to the west, and the Tilbury industrial lands to the south-west.
Where townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere. There is no residential land on the island to map.

Transit is industrial-edge only: route 340 runs Scottsdale Exchange to 22nd Street Station via Scott Road, Highway 91, the Alex Fraser Bridge and the Cliveden Interchange, serving the island's industrial area edge; no bus exchange on the island itself was confirmed.
North Delta is a SnapStats-covered community; Annacis Island simply has no residential row in it.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Annacis Island

items.t: Why there are no townhouse rules to apply on the island itself: the governing layer is industrial. The Delta OCP 2024 (Bylaw No. 8400, consolidated, no lettered schedules) designates Annacis Island industrial, and port-terminal parcels are also subject to Vancouver Fraser Port Authority permitting — the approval path for a parcel depends on which regime it sits under, and neither regime is residential townhouse development.

SSMUH does not create island housing: Delta's small-scale multi-unit housing Bylaws No. 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024, allow four units on residential properties (six within 400 m of frequent transit along Scott Road, in North Delta) — they apply to residential land, and Annacis Island has none.

If a buyer pivots to a North Delta strata townhouse instead (the nearest real stock), the BC standard block applies: Form B diligence under Strata Property Act s. 59 (fees, amounts owing, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page).

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata, general): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote; since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Rental and age bylaws (strata, general): rental-restriction bylaws are VOID since November 24, 2022 — any directory line saying "rentals not allowed" for a BC strata is void in-entry; only 55+ age bylaws remain valid (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Fee-simple contrast (general): a fee-simple townhouse carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees — municipal rules and any registered covenants/HOA only. No fee-simple townhouse exists on Annacis Island because no townhouse of any tenure exists here.

blocks.text: Good to know about Annacis Island

items.t: The auto terminal got bigger, not smaller: the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority's Annacis Auto Terminal Optimization Project, in partnership with Wallenius Wilhelmsen, consolidated the Annacis and Richmond auto terminals into the Annacis facility and enabled it to handle up to 480,000 vehicles annually — a 36% increase in capacity — with on-terminal works complete in early 2025 per the port authority's timeline. That is the island's growth story, and it is industrial.

The region's sewage is treated here: Metro Vancouver's Annacis Island Wastewater Treatment Plant is a secondary treatment plant serving the Fraser Sewerage Area — a permanent, high-activity industrial neighbour that shapes truck traffic and odour expectations for nearby industrial units, and one more reason the island is not housing land.

Two governments touch an island parcel: island land can be City-zoned industrial land or Port of Vancouver terminal land (the auto terminal at 820 Dock Road is designated "Port Terminal" under a port authority permit, PER-21-019) — establish which regime a parcel sits under before drafting anything.

Delta's industrial base is regionally significant: 1,527 hectares of industrially zoned and designated land in Metro Vancouver's 2020 Regional Industrial Lands Inventory, approximately 13% of the region's inventory — Annacis Island is one of its four named homes (with River Road East, Tilbury Industrial Park and Roberts Bank).

There is no school catchment to check because there are no homes: no public school on the island was confirmed in School District 37 material, and SD37 catchments are address-based through the School Locator — an island address has no residential population to catchment. Families shopping "Annacis" are really shopping North Delta catchments.

The bridge is the whole commute case: access is Highway 91 via the Cliveden Interchange and the Alex Fraser Bridge, into the business park via Chester Road / Audley Boulevard and Cliveden Avenue — the same corridor route 340 uses. Published drive times: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Annacis Island

items.t: What trades instead — industrial lots: freehold industrial lots and strata industrial units in the Annacis Business Park, plus port-terminal land at the Annacis Auto Terminal. Where a strata plan is filed, BC strata guidance applies — owners own their strata lots and together own common property as a strata corporation.

Fee-simple as the default land form: outside the strata industrial complexes, island land is fee-simple industrial land — the default form for land generally — held for logistics, warehousing, automotive-sector and service-industrial use. No named fee-simple bare-land subdivision was verified by an official or developer source in the research; no subdivision is named here rather than inventing one.

Lot character — UNVERIFIED, not filled in: industrial parcel standards are UNVERIFIED — the industrial zone names and minimum lot standards for Annacis parcels in Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 were not confirmed from a City zone sheet in the research.

Named industrial anchors — not land inventory: the Annacis Auto Terminal, at 820 Dock Road, is a Port of Vancouver terminal; the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority's project permit for the terminal lists the land use designation as "Port Terminal" and the tenant as WWL Vehicle Services Canada, Ltd. (Wallenius Wilhelmsen). Metro Vancouver's Annacis Island Wastewater Treatment Plant is also on the island; Metro Vancouver lists Annacis Island among its secondary treatment plants (with Lulu Island and Northwest Langley), and the plant serves the Fraser Sewerage Area. Both are operating industrial/port land, documented as land-use context — never as for-sale inventory.

Port project — documented as a project, never inventory: the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority led the Annacis Auto Terminal Optimization Project in partnership with Wallenius Wilhelmsen, consolidating the Annacis and Richmond auto terminals into the Annacis facility and enabling it to handle up to 480,000 vehicles annually — a 36% increase in capacity; the port authority's timeline shows on-terminal works complete in early 2025. This is a completed port expansion on port land, not a lot offering.
ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve residential land was confirmed on the island — the island's documented position is non-ALR industrial ground, and no ALR split is stated.

Serviced vs unserviced: parcel-level servicing (municipal water/sewer connection status for a single island lot) is UNCONFIRMED in the research and is not asserted here; confirm with the City and on title for the specific parcel. No well/septic position is documented for island industrial ground in the research.

Land assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: none documented in the research for Annacis Island — no assembly, development site or rezoning proposal is named, and none is presented as for-sale inventory.

Market figures: the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report contains no Annacis Island sub-area row — its Delta coverage is the North Delta community and its four residential sub-areas only — so no SnapStats figures exist for Annacis Island in this report, and none are presented here. Industrial market figures (rents, vacancy, land values): UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Annacis Island

items.t: Annacis Island is an island in the Fraser River, in the City of Delta, in the Highway 91 / Alex Fraser Bridge corridor; the island is bounded by the Fraser River channels around it (Annacis Channel / Annieville Channel), and street access is by Derwent Way, Cliveden Avenue, Eaton Way and Audley Boulevard.
Nearby areas: Nordel and the rest of North Delta to the south across the Alex Fraser Bridge, New Westminster to the north, Richmond to the west, Tilbury industrial lands to the south-west.

Roads and commute: Highway 91 via the Cliveden Interchange and the Alex Fraser Bridge; access into Annacis Business Park is via Chester Road / Audley Boulevard and Cliveden Avenue; Highway 91 connects to the Highway 99 and Highway 17 routes.

Transit: route 340 runs Scottsdale Exchange to 22nd Street Station via Scott Road, 64 Avenue, Kittson Parkway, Highway 91, the Alex Fraser Bridge and the Cliveden Interchange, serving the Annacis Island industrial area edge; no bus exchange on the island itself was confirmed.

Schools: no public school on Annacis Island was confirmed in School District 37 material; SD37 catchments are address-based through the SD37 School Locator, and the island has no residential population to catchment.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Annacis Island

items.t: Two approval regimes: island parcels can be City-zoned industrial land or Port of Vancouver terminal land (the auto terminal at 820 Dock Road is designated "Port Terminal" under a port authority permit), and the approval path differs — establish which regime the parcel sits under before drafting.

Flood / dike diligence: the island is riverfront industrial land surrounded by Fraser River channels; the City of Delta operates and maintains flood protection infrastructure including dikes, seawalls and foreshore protection, and is the diking authority with over 63 kilometres of flood protection infrastructure citywide; dyke and floodplain detail for specific parcels: UNVERIFIED — confirm Flood Construction Level, dike setbacks and any flood covenants on title early.

ALR rules: For completeness where a Delta buyer looks at ALR ground elsewhere: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps are principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Strata rules where a strata industrial lot is bought (the BC strata block — it applies to the lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children) — a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. None of this creates a residential use on industrial land.

blocks.text: Good to know about Annacis Island

items.t: The auto terminal got bigger, not quieter: the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority's Annacis Auto Terminal Optimization Project consolidated the Annacis and Richmond auto terminals into the Annacis facility, enabling it to handle up to 480,000 vehicles annually — a 36% increase in capacity — with on-terminal works complete in early 2025.

Delta holds a disproportionate share of the region's industrial land: the OCP cites 1,527 hectares of industrially zoned and designated land in Delta, approximately 13% of Metro Vancouver's 2020 Regional Industrial Lands Inventory — policy pressure runs toward keeping islands like this industrial, not converting them to housing.

No park, school, shop or grocery store on the island was confirmed in official sources — consistent with no residential population; the nearest hospital is Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, Delta, in Ladner (Fraser Health); the North Delta Public Health Unit is at 11245 84 Avenue, Delta.

BCIT has a campus on the island — and still points students off-island for housing: BCIT's Annacis Island Campus page lists off-campus housing resources and hotels in surrounding areas (New Westminster, North Delta, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam) rather than any on-island accommodation.

faq.a: No. No residential housing mix was confirmed on the island; the Delta Official Community Plan treats the island as industrial land, home to the Annacis Business Park, the Port of Vancouver auto terminal and Metro Vancouver's wastewater treatment plant.

faq.q: How is the island reached by road?
faq.a: By Highway 91 and the Alex Fraser Bridge via the Cliveden Interchange, with park access via Chester Road / Audley Boulevard and Cliveden Avenue, as shown on the TransLink 340 route description.

faq.q: What is the Annacis Auto Terminal?
faq.a: It is the Port of Vancouver's vehicle terminal at 820 Dock Road on Annacis Island, operated by Wallenius Wilhelmsen; the port authority's optimization project consolidated the Annacis and Richmond auto terminals there, lifting capacity to 480,000 vehicles annually.

faq.q: Is there a bus route serving the island?
faq.a: Route 340 runs between Scottsdale Exchange and 22nd Street Station via Highway 91 and the Cliveden Interchange, serving the industrial area edge; no bus exchange on the island itself was confirmed.

faq.q: Which plan governs land use on the island?
faq.a: The Delta Official Community Plan 2024, Bylaw No. 8400, which covers land use across Delta including industrial areas; port-terminal land is also subject to Vancouver Fraser Port Authority permitting.

faq.q: Can I buy a townhouse on Annacis Island?
faq.a: No — there is none to buy. The island is industrial land under the Delta OCP 2024, and the research confirms no residential housing mix on it at all. The nearest townhouse stock is in North Delta, on the mainland south of the Alex Fraser Bridge.

faq.q: But I saw strata units listed in the Annacis Business Park — aren't those townhouses?
faq.a: No. Those are strata industrial units — warehouse/industrial strata lots whose owners together own the common property as a strata corporation. Same Act, completely different product: no home, no residential use.

faq.q: Could the island be rezoned residential one day?
faq.a: No source read signals that: the current OCP (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) designates the island industrial and names it among the places Delta's industries are primarily located, and the port auto terminal was expanded, not wound down. Any future change is UNCONFIRMED speculation — do not price it.

faq.q: Where do people who work on the island actually live?
faq.a: The residential areas across the bridge: Nordel and the rest of North Delta to the south, New Westminster to the north, Richmond to the west. Route 340 connects Scottsdale Exchange to 22nd Street Station via the island's edge, which is the transit link island workers use.

faq.q: If I buy a strata townhouse in North Delta instead, what document matters most?
faq.a: The Form B Information Certificate — fees, amounts owing, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary and the most recent depreciation report — plus two years of strata records. It is the diligence package a strata purchase turns on.

faq.q: Is there any residential land to buy on Annacis Island?
faq.a: No. No residential housing mix was confirmed on the island; the Delta OCP treats the island as industrial land, home to the Annacis Business Park, the Port of Vancouver auto terminal and Metro Vancouver's wastewater treatment plant.

faq.q: What land actually trades here, then?
faq.a: Freehold industrial lots and strata industrial units in the Annacis Business Park, plus port-terminal land — industrial land, not house lots.

faq.q: I saw a strata lot for sale in the business park — is that a bare-land strata house lot?
faq.a: No. It is a strata industrial lot: strata tenure applies (Form B, fees, bylaws), but the use is warehouse/industrial, not a residential lot you can live on.
